master.title: Azerbaijan Press Review - 17/02/2022
master.content:
AZERBAIJAN DAILY PRESS REVIEW

Subject: Main headlines in Azerbaijan on 17/02/2022

Political headlines

Coronavirus

·       Azerbaijan confirms 7,148 more COVID-19 cases. On 16 February, Azerbaijan detected 7,148 new COVID-19 cases, 7,387 persons recovered, and 22 persons died. To date, 759,753 persons have been infected with coronavirus in the country. Among those, 703,952 persons have recovered, and 9,127 persons have died. Currently, there are 46,674 active cases. Since the start of the vaccination, 12,627,370 vaccine doses have been administered in Azerbaijan (5,273,971 persons received the first dose, 4,768,299 persons the second dose and 2,585,100 persons the booster dose). (16/02/2022       Trend, more; more)

 

Foreign Affairs

·       EU: "Funds on ATAF are in line with Azerbaijan's five national priorities". "The funds allocated under the Administrative Agreement on the Azerbaijan Technical Assistance Facility (ATAF) project signed by the European Union (EU) and the World Bank (WB) are in conformity with the five national priorities set by Azerbaijan," Head of the EU Delegation to Azerbaijan Peter Michalko said. According to him, the project will be effective in mitigating the effects of the pandemic. "The ATAF project is designed as a platform of quick steps and will help the government take more dynamic steps. The success of this initiative is our success," he said. (16/02/2022       Report, more)

·       President of Poland holds phone talks with Azerbaijani President. On 16 February, President of the Republic of Poland Andrzej Duda made a phone call to President Aliyev. During the phone talk, the sides exchanged views on the development of bilateral relations between Azerbaijan and Poland in various fields. As the OSCE Chairman, the Polish President touched upon the security issues in the Central and Eastern European region and underlined that the steps taken within the OSCE would serve to reduce tensions. They also exchanged views on the developments around Ukraine. (16.02.2022 Trend, more)

·       Azerbaijani, Russian FMs discuss implementation of tripartite statements. A telephone conversation took place between the foreign ministers of Azerbaijan - Jeyhun Bayramov and Russia - Sergey Lavrov. The ministers considered topical issues on the agenda of mutual cooperation. Given that 2022 marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two states, the parties exchanged opinions on the events to be organized related to it. The ministers also discussed the situation in the region, including issues on the implementation of tripartite statements. The sides talked about the current situation around Ukraine, and also addressed the issues of cooperation within Azerbaijan's chairmanship at the OSCE Forum for Security Cooperation. (16.02.2022 Trend, more)

·       Turkish FM's visit to Azerbaijan postponed. In a phone conversation, Turkish Foreign Minister Çavuşoğlu informed Minister Bayramov about the postponement of his visit to Azerbaijan since he was infected with COVID-19. (16.02.2022 APA, more)

·       AZAL makes payment to Armenia for flights to Nakhchivan. National carrier of Azerbaijan, Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL) has paid about 32,000 euro to Armenia for air navigation services, according to the Civil Aviation Committee of Armenia. It is noted that from 6 October 2021, AZAL started to use the air space of Armenia for the implementation of passenger flights to Nakhchivan. (16.02.2022 APA, more)

·       US, Azerbaijan working to increase the number of exchange programmes for students. The US and Azerbaijan are trying to increase the number of exchange programmes for students, US Ambassador to Azerbaijan Earle Litzenberger told the local media representatives. "We have over 500 Azerbaijani students studying in the US. I would love to see this figure raising to 5,000. I think it is one of the best programmes we have in place, to lay the foundation for the next 30 years of our relationship. We strongly support expanding opportunities for people-to-people exchanges on English language instruction" said the ambassador. (16.02.2022 Trend, more)

·       Azerbaijani delegation to visit Armenia. According to Armenian media, an Azerbaijani delegation will attend a meeting of the Euronest Parliament Assembly Bureau, which will be held in Yerevan on 19-22 February. Azerbaijani side has expressed initial agreement for participation in the meeting of the Euronest Parliament Assembly Bureau. (16.02.2022 APA, more)

·       Azerbaijani parliamentarians to pay working visit to UAE. Chairman of the Milli Majlis Committee on Economic Policy, Industry and Entrepreneurship Tahir Mirkishili, Chairman of the Committee on Culture Ganira Pashayeva, MPs Soltan Mammadov, Mahir Abbaszada and Elnur Allahverdiyev will visit Dubai (UAE) on 17 February. During the working visit, the parliamentarians will hold a number of meetings, exchange views on expanding cooperation between the countries in the economic, cultural, humanitarian spheres, and developing parliamentary ties. (16/02/2022       Report, more)

 

·       The US is not happy with the media law. The way the new law "On Media" was adopted is "disappointing", said US Ambassador to Azerbaijan Lee Litsenberger. During the work on the draft law, the opinions of all interested parties and the proposals of experts were not taken into account in order to improve this document. The US Embassy is in close contact with government officials, media and journalists. "We have been open about our concerns. Much will depend on how this law is applied in practice. If the authorities use it to restrict freedom of the press, it will be very disappointing. If the authorities will use the law as they promise - to raise the level of the press and the professionalism of journalists, this is another matter," the ambassador said. (16/02/2022       Turan, more)

 

Karabakh

·       New World Bank - EU project may also cover the regained territories. "Azerbaijan Technical Assistance Facility (ATAF) is a technical assistance project, and if requested by the Azerbaijani government, the project will also share its experiences regarding the restoration process in the retaken areas," said Sarah Michael Country Manager for World Bank in Azerbaijan. Notably, the Azerbaijan Technical Assistance Facility (ATAF) has a total budget of 5.25 million euros, and this three-year programme is funded by the EU and managed by the World Bank. (16.02.2022 APA, more)

·       Types of mines planted by Armenians in the regained territories. Chairman of the Board of ANAMA Vugar Suleymanov noted that among the discovered mines, plastic mines are more common. "The majority are anti-personnel mines of Armenian production, that is, PMN-G, as well as mines PMN-2, PMD-6, PMP, and from anti-tank mines - mainly TM-57, TM-62M, TM-62P, TM-62P2, TM- 62P3. At the same time, the enemy set a large number of booby traps against the civilian population and the army - mines and improvised explosive devices (IEDs)," Vugar Suleymanov emphasized. (16.02.2022 Report, more)

 

Domestic News

 

·       Azerbaijan reveals number of its citizens repatriated from the EU. Over 40 Azerbaijani citizens were repatriated under the readmission agreement with the EU on 15 February, the State Migration Service of Azerbaijan told. According to the service, 39 Azerbaijani citizens were repatriated from Germany and three from Austria. (16/02/2022       Trend, more)

·       Azerbaijan considers proposals for improving municipal administration. The Ministry of Justice has sent a package of proposals to the Cabinet of Ministers on improvement of municipal administration, efficient use of municipal lands, elimination of challenges in the collection of local taxes and payments. This is envisaged by the annual report of the agency exercising administrative control over the activities of municipalities. (16/02/2022       Trend, more)

·       State Service: There will be nine non-working days in Azerbaijan around Novruz. "According to decision of the Cabinet of Ministers "On the determination of dates of Novruz, Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha for 2022," March 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 of 2022 is Novruz Holiday," said head of press service of State Labour Inspection Aynur Osmangizi. Thus, as March 19, 26, 27 coincide with Saturday and Sunday, 9 consecutive days (March 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27) will be non-working days. (16/02/2022       Trend, more)


 
Economic News

·       European companies invested over $20 billion in Azerbaijan in nine years. "Over the past nine years, European companies have invested over $20 billion in Azerbaijan," Azerbaijan's First Deputy Economy Minister Elnur Aliyev told at the ceremony organised on the occasion of the signature of the Administrative Agreement on the Azerbaijan Technical Assistance Facility (ATAF) project. According to him, Azerbaijan closely cooperates with the European Union within the Eastern Partnership: "Azerbaijan has implemented about 55 twinning projects within the Eastern Partnership programme. We also cooperate with the World Bank in transport, agriculture, social and other fields. So far, the World Bank has provided technical assistance to Azerbaijan worth about $20 million on 96 projects." (16/02/2022      Report, more; more; more)

 

Social Media

·       Social media users write about truck drivers protest: The videos of four trucks, which have blocked the movement at Heydar Aliyev avenue since last night, have been trending the social networks. Trucks displayed a banner with accusations against the head of the Automobile Transport Agency Anar Rzayev and the chief of the agency's department for rejecting transport permits. The absolute majority of users expressed support for the truck drivers accusing the government officials of corruption and racketeering. Users applauded the protest expressing relief that the "people are finally starting to wake up to demand the respect for their rights". Users note that the negligence and gluttony of officials have pushed people over the edge and state the need to dismiss and punish the corrupt officials, which do nothing but embezzle the state budget. Users note that at the time when the country experiences economic stagnation and the state budget is replenished through taxes and fines imposed on the population, the racketeering of officials is equal to treason. Users conclude that the government must closely watch and work to prevent such small cases as small protests tend to turn into big protest.

 

 

Please note that this press review includes information published by different sources and does not represent the views of the Delegation.

candidate.title: DAILY DEVELOPMENTS IN TAJIKISTAN, 17 February 2022
candidate.content:
EUROPEAN UNION

Delegation to the Republic of Tajikistan

 

Political, Press and Information Section

 


 

DAILY DEVELOPMENTS IN TAJIKISTAN, 17 February 2022

MAIN HEADLINES

·       EU supports opening first teachers learning innovation center in Dushanbe

·       Heritage Foundation ranks Tajikistan among countries with repressive economics

·       Exports of Iran to Tajikistan soar

·       Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan agreed to regulate borders without participation of third party

·       More than 4 tons of drugs seized in Tajikistan in 2021

 

EU supports opening first teachers learning innovation center in Dushanbe

European Union, the United Nations Children Fund (UNICEF) in Tajikistan together with the Ministry of Education and Science of the Republic of Tajikistan (MoES) held the official opening ceremony of the first national teachers learning innovation center for the production of education TV lessons and the promotion of innovative blended learning content within the European Union funded program on Quality Education Support Program II. The European Union Delegation to Tajikistan says the teachers learning innovation center opened its doors at the premises of Republican Institute for In-Service Teachers Training under the MoES.  The ergonomic and child-friendly design of the studio is reportedly equipped with video-production and other teaching and learning tools, as well as modern software and hardware. UNICEF in Tajikistan and European Union are supporting the MoES in the development of innovative mechanisms to ensure the continuity of learning for every child and adolescent in the country during COVID 19 pandemic (Asia Plus/EU Delegation)

Heritage Foundation ranks Tajikistan among countries with repressive economics

The international research institute Heritage Foundation, together with The Wall Street Journal, published the Index of Economic Freedom-2022 (Index of Economic Freedom-2022). Tajikistan is on the 147th place among 177 countries of the world that are included in the rating. The countries of the world, depending on the level of economic freedom, are divided into 5 categories - from "free" to "repressive". Tajikistan, along with Turkmenistan (165th place), as well as another 30 countries of the world (North Korea, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cuba and others), is in the lowest basket . The authors of the rating note that the five-year downward trend in economic freedom continues in Tajikistan. They specifically highlight the "strong weakness of investment and financial freedom" in the republic (Asia Plus).

Exports of Iran to Tajikistan soar

Iran's exports to Tajikistan increased by 143% in terms of value and 157% in terms of volume, during the first six months of the current Iranian year (March 21 through September 22, 2021), compared to the same period last Iranian year, the Spokesman for the Islamic Republic of Iran Customs Administration (IRICA) Rouhollah Latifi said. The official stressed that Iran exported 22,000 tons of goods worth $17 million to Tajikistan within the mentioned period. "Furthermore, Iran imported $4.7 million worth of goods from Tajikistan in 6 months. The imports increased by 16%, compared to the same period last Iranian year," he added. Latifi noted that Tajikistan ranks 9th in Iran's exports to the member states of Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) and 8th in Iran s imports from these states (Trend.az).

Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan agreed to regulate borders without participation of third party

Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Akylbek Zhaparov during a press conference commented on the issue of delimitation and demarcation of the state border of Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. He said that the borders are recognized when two neighbours agree. President Sadyr Zhaparov, during his trip to Beijing, said that he and the president of Tajikistan had instructed the Ministries of Foreign Affairs to start negotiations on the border. Negotiations have now begun and are already intensively under way. Earlier, these negotiations were interrupted due to the conflict at the border, but negotiations have been resumed now. Both presidents agreed that they would be able to regulate this issue without a third party, Zhaparov said (Trend.az).

More than 4 tons of drugs seized in Tajikistan in 2021

In 2021, 4 tons 83 kg 274 g of narcotic drugs were seized in the country, which is 68.4% or 1 ton 658 kg 36 g more than in 2020, General Major Khabibullo Vohidzoda. According to him, in 2021, compared to 2020, the seizure of heroin increased 2.1 times, hashish - 2.3 times, but opium and cannabis decreased - by 24.7% and 10.4%, respectively. "In 2021, law enforcement agencies seized 106 kg of psychotropic substances, which is 2.4 times or 63 kg more than in 2020," Vohidzoda said (Asia Plus).
